newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN CASH COFFEE BUYERS RESIST HIGHER PRICES.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN CASH COFFEE BUYERS RESIST HIGHER PRICES.

text.p: Physical coffee buyers in Germany said they were unmoved by the strength of prices on the New York arabica futures market.
It reflected nearby North American tightness and speculation rather than global fundamentals, they argued on Monday.
"There is no demand for spot coffee priced against the September contract here," one said.
"Certified stocks in New York on the other hands are not sufficient to cover the September open position -- so we've got two separate markets on both sides of the Atlantic."
New York ended mixed on Friday with September down 2.95 cents/lb at 205.85 and December up 1.60 at 177.85.
Traders found no positive price incentive from reports that cooler weather was expected this week in Brazil.
Importers reported some sales of Dec/Jan Central American, East African and New Guinea arabicas.
Demand for new crop arabicas was generally muted, and buyers and sellers were unable to agree on prices, they said.
Robusta supplies were ample but buyers thought prices were too firm.
Where business emerged, West African robustas sold better than Asian origins.
Second hand Brazils were nominally quoted for Sept shipment at $178, Colombians at $208 and Guatemalans at $240.
Indonesian robustas rose to $80 on the week from $77 cif second hand while Cameroon robustas were newly quoted at $79.
